The provided text contains language that is generally considered outdated and potentially offensive in modern accessibility contexts. The phrase "the blind" is a form of person-first language violation; it defines individuals solely by their disability rather than as people with a disability. Inclusive language guidelines recommend using "people who are blind" or "blind people" to emphasize personhood first. Additionally, while the features mentioned (tactile floor plans and audio descriptions) are excellent accessibility accommodations, the framing of the audience as a monolithic group ("the blind") can be seen as exclusionary.

The color of a common crow is black.
